trails.title: From the hit single to the control room
trails.description: Follow one career across a pop duo, a record label and a singer-songwriter breakthrough.

steps.title: A familiar name on another sleeve
steps.text: Start with Peter & Gordon’s A World Without Love. Follow the writing credit back to McCartney.

steps.title: The job changes
steps.text: In 1968 Asher became Apple’s head of A&R. Taylor’s debut puts his name behind the record as producer.

steps.title: Another room, another sound
steps.text: Move to Sweet Baby James. Compare the arrangements with the debut; listen to where the guitar and voice sit.

trails.title: One song, three different jobs
trails.description: See why every line needs a role.

steps.title: The writer
steps.text: King wrote You’ve Got a Friend. Start here to follow the song itself.

steps.title: The interpretation
steps.text: Taylor recorded it. Compare his phrasing with King’s own version.

steps.title: Behind the recording
steps.text: Asher produced Taylor’s version. The production line describes a separate job from the writing line.

trails.title: A singer’s record can be a songwriter map
trails.description: Look through the voice on the cover to the writers inside.

steps.title: Choose the record
steps.text: Open Heart Like a Wheel, then trace the producer connection to Asher.

steps.title: Follow the partnership
steps.text: Their collaboration continues on Hasten Down the Wind, released two years later.

steps.title: Read past the cover
steps.text: Now follow Bonoff and Zevon. Listen to how one voice brings different writers into the same album.

trails.title: A harmony thread crosses the Atlantic
trails.description: Two kinds of connection can sound alike while meaning different things.

steps.title: An influence you can listen for
steps.text: Asher named the Everly Brothers as an inspiration. Compare the pairs’ close harmonies.

steps.title: The song travels too
steps.text: Ronstadt later recorded When Will I Be Loved. Follow a repertoire connection to Heart Like a Wheel.

editorialNotes: Four album tiles are intended as typographic sleeves rather than unlicensed cover images.
Performance means an actual recording or group membership. Production, songwriting, career and influence must remain distinguishable in the interface.

The McCartney debut credit deliberately says played: the primary GRAMMY interview supports participation but does not name the instrument. Do not upgrade this edge to bass without a separate credit source.
The Everlys-to-duo edge is documented influence, not a recording credit; label it clearly.

Heart Like a Wheel is credited solely to Anna McGarrigle in many catalogues; Linda’s official biography calls it a McGarrigle sisters song. No writer edge for this title is added here because of that inconsistency.
Node and edge years refer to the displayed record or career event, not full lifespan or complete collaboration range.
Editorial listening prompts are suggestions, not historical claims about similarity.
everlys-linda is deliberately career/repertoire, not songwriting by the duo: the official Everly Brothers history identifies Phil Everly as the writer.
description: A hit-making singer, a record-label scout, a producer. Follow the people, songs and sessions around Peter Asher. Every line has a role; every story opens its source.
